questions.question: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 2 : 3. If this ratio is required to be 7 : 9 then the quantity of Milk to be added further will be-
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **Milk** : **Water** = 2 : 3. To keep water constant for the 7 : 9 target, multiply initial ratio by 3.

New Initial Ratio = (2 × 3) : (3 × 3) = 6 : 9. Final Ratio = 7 : 9.

Initial total parts = 6 + 9 = 15 units. Given 15 units = 60 L ⇒ 1 unit = 4 L.

Increase in Milk = 7 − 6 = 1 unit.

Added Milk = 1 × 4 L = 4 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 L.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total **Mixture** = 60 L, Initial **Ratio** (Milk : Water) = 2 : 3.

**Formula:** Quantity = [Ratio Part ÷ Total Parts] × Total Quantity

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a80ab5ec18b0ab4113fb8ac1f2cfd125f4bed9370598d4019e982283134b978.png] 

⇒ Initial Milk = (2 / 5) × 60 = 24 L

⇒ Initial Water = (3 / 5) × 60 = 36 L

⇒ Let the quantity of **Milk** added be 'x' L.

⇒ New Milk = 24 + x

⇒ New Ratio = (24 + x) / 36 = 7 / 9

⇒ 9 × (24 + x) = 7 × 36

⇒ 216 + 9x = 252

⇒ 9x = 252 − 216 = 36

⇒ x = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 L

**∴ The correct answer is 4 L.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Quantity Rule

When only one component is added to a mixture, the quantity of the other component remains constant. Equating the constant parts in ratios simplifies calculations.

Ratio and Proportion

If a : b is the ratio, then total parts = a + b. Each part's value = (Total Quantity) ÷ (a + b).

Replacement vs. Addition

In addition, the total volume increases. In replacement, some mixture is removed and replaced by a component, keeping total volume constant.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a cricket bat whose marked price is Rs. 30, at a discount of 15%, and gives a ball costing Rs. 1.50 free with each bat. Even then he makes a profit of 20%. his cost price, per bat is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net Revenue (Effective SP) = (85% of 30) − Cost of free item

Effective SP = 25.50 − 1.50 = Rs. 24

Profit = 20% ⇒ CP = Effective SP ÷ 1.2

CP = 24 ÷ 1.2 = Rs. 20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price** (MP) of the bat = Rs. 30

**Discount** = 15%

Cost of free **ball** = Rs. 1.50

**Profit percentage** = 20%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ae239d1d4e952efe3b60fa6db34947d26f8926ba0741acb700b6884f984443f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount amount on bat = 15% of 30 = (15 ÷ 100) × 30 = Rs. 4.50

⇒ Amount collected from customer = 30 − 4.50 = Rs. 25.50

⇒ Effective Selling Price (SP) = Amount collected − Cost of free item

⇒ Effective SP = 25.50 − 1.50 = Rs. 24.00

⇒ Profit = 20% on CP

⇒ CP × (1 + 20 ÷ 100) = 24

⇒ CP × 1.2 = 24

⇒ CP = 24 ÷ 1.2 = Rs. 20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This formula is used when no extra free items are given.

Effective Selling Price

When a free item is given, the cost of that item must be subtracted from the actual SP to find the net revenue earned by the seller.

Basic Profit Formula

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.</p

questions.question: The slant height and radius of a right circular cone are in the ratio 29 ∶ 20. If its volume is 4838.4 π cm³, then its radius is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given ratio of Slant height (l) : Radius (r) = 29 : 20.

Using Pythagorean triplet (20, 21, 29), the height (h) corresponds to 21 parts.

Volume part = 1/3 × r² × h = 1/3 × 20² × 21 = 2800 units³.

Comparing with actual volume: x³ = 4838.4 / 2800 = 1.728 ⇒ x = 1.2.

Radius (r) = 20 × 1.2 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of l : r = 29 : 20

Volume of cone (V) = 4838.4 π cm³

**Formula:**

Volume of cone = (1/3) π r² h

Relation between l, r, and h: l² = r² + h²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3fb185ab9f9f63f34bfeb38ae83f596f0fb75ec374d80fb0ec2d9d78ca0449c.png] 

Let common ratio be x. Then r = 20x and l = 29x.

⇒ h = √(l² − r²) = √((29x)² − (20x)²)

⇒ h = √(841x² − 400x²) = √(441x²) = 21x

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × (20x)² × (21x) = 4838.4 π

⇒ (1/3) × 400x² × 21x = 4838.4

⇒ 400 × 7x³ = 4838.4

⇒ 2800x³ = 4838.4

⇒ x³ = 4838.4 ÷ 2800 = 1.728

⇒ x = ³√1.728 = 1.2

⇒ Radius (r) = 20x = 20 × 1.2 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Cone

The lateral surface area or CSA of a right circular cone is given by the formula CSA = πrl, where r is radius and l is slant height.

Total Surface Area of Cone

The TSA includes the base area and the curved surface area, calculated as TSA = πr(r + l).

Pythagorean Relation in Cones

In any right circular cone, the height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) always satisfy the right-angled triangle property l² = r² + h².</p

questions.question: The base of right pyramid is an equilateral triangle, each side of which is 20 cm. Each slant edge is 30 cm. The vertical height (in cm) of the pyramid is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a right pyramid with an equilateral triangle base, Height² = (Slant Edge)² − (Circumradius of base)².

Circumradius (R) = side / √3 = 20 / √3 cm.

Height² = 30² − (20/√3)² = 900 − 400/3 = 2300/3.

Height = √(2300 / 3) = 10√(23/3) cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 10√(23/3) cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of equilateral base (a) = 20 cm

Slant edge (e) = 30 cm

**Formula Used:**

Vertical Height (h) = √[e² − R²], where R is the circumradius of the base.

For an equilateral triangle, Circumradius (R) = a / √3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c8c117d14d4126872ade36aba9caa7308fbcc9dbb3584ff6ae9783c8e2e6b60.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 20 / √3 cm

⇒ h² = e² − R²

⇒ h² = 30² − (20 / √3)²

⇒ h² = 900 − 400 / 3

⇒ h² = (2700 − 400) / 3

⇒ h² = 2300 / 3

⇒ h = √(2300 / 3) = 10√(23/3) cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10√(23/3) cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of any pyramid is given by 1/3 × Base Area × Vertical Height.

Slant Height vs Slant Edge

Slant height (l) is the height of the triangular face, while slant edge (e) is the length of the edge connecting the vertex to a base corner. Relation: l² = h² + r² (where r = in-radius).

Lateral Surface Area

Lateral Surface Area of a right pyramid = 1/2 × Perimeter of base × Slant height (l).

Equilateral Triangle Radii

For side a, Circumradius R = a/√3 and In-radius r = a/(2√3).</p

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 82 days, B can do in 123 days and C can do the same work alone in 164 days. questions.question: If the expression x³ + 3x² + 4x + k has a factor x + 5, then what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If (x + 5) is a factor, then substituting x = −5 must make the expression zero.

Expression: (−5)³ + 3(−5)² + 4(−5) + k = 0

−125 + 3(25) − 20 + k = 0

−145 + 75 + k = 0 ⇒ k − 70 = 0

k = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Polynomial P(x) = x³ + 3x² + 4x + k and a factor (x + 5).

Formula Used: Factor Theorem states that if (x + a) is a factor of P(x), then P(−a) = 0.

⇒ Let the factor be x + 5 = 0, which gives x = −5.

⇒ Substitute x = −5 into the polynomial P(x):

⇒ P(−5) = (−5)³ + 3(−5)² + 4(−5) + k = 0

⇒ −125 + 3(25) − 20 + k = 0

⇒ −125 + 75 − 20 + k = 0

⇒ (−125 − 20) + 75 + k = 0

⇒ −145 + 75 + k = 0

⇒ −70 + k = 0

⇒ k = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Additional Information__**

Factor Theorem

A polynomial f(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if f(a) = 0. This is a special case of the remainder theorem.

Remainder Theorem

When a polynomial f(x) is divided by a linear divisor (x − a), the remainder of the division is f(a).

Synthetic Division

A shorthand method of polynomial division, especially when dividing by a linear factor of the form (x − a).

Roots of Polynomials

If x = r is a root of P(x) = 0, then (x − r) is exactly divisible by P(x), meaning the remainder is zero.</p

questions.question: All the Kings, Queens and Aces are removed from a pack of 52 cards, The remaining cards are well shuffled and then a card is drawn from it. Find the probability that the card drawn is a black face card?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

All the Kings, Queens and Aces are removed from a pack of 52 cards.

**Concept:**

In a deck of 52 cards, there are 4 suits of cards: Hearts, Clubs, Diamonds & Sprades. 

Each suit contains 13 cards including 1 King, 1 Queen, 1 Jack & 1 Ace.

King, Queen and Jack are called Face cards.

The Ace value is 1.

Diamonds and Hearts are red coloured and Spades and Clubs are black coloured.

**Formula used:**

P(A) = n(A) over n(S)

where, P(A) = Probability of event 'A'

n(A) = Total no. of favourable outcomes

n(S) = Total no. of events

**Calculation:**

Total no. of Queens = 4

Total no. of Kings = 4

Total no. of Aces = 4

So, the total no. of cards removed from a deck of 52 cards = (4 + 4 +4) = 12

Now, Total no. of events, **n(S)** = 52 - 12 = 40

According to the given data, black face Kings and Queens are removed already.

Now, Total no. of remaining Black Face Card = Total no. of Jacks in Spades suit and Clubs suit = 1 + 1 = 2

So, No. of favourable outcomes, **n(A)** = 2

Probability of a Black Face Card, **P(A)** = 2/40 = 1/20

**∴ The probability of the card drawn is a black face card is 1/20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__** The total no. of favourable outcomes will be no. of black face Jacks, not all the black cards (except Kings and Queens).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__** Face card means King, Queen and Jack only.

questions.question: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25,500 at the end of three years is Rs. 8,440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Amount to Principal for 3 years = (25500 + 8440.50) ÷ 25500 = 33940.5 ÷ 25500 = 1331 / 1000.

Equivalent ratio for 1 year = ³√(1331 / 1000) = 11 / 10.

Interest rate (R) = (11 − 10) ÷ 10 × 100% = 10%.

Simple Interest for 3 years = 30% of Principal = 30% of 25500 = 7650.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 25,500

Time (T) = 3 years

Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 8,440.50

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R / 100)T

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5bd21ce14ea0293048f35b60ce53547b23061c619f85919d7bf9a24893ee5a4c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount (A) = P + CI

⇒ A = 25500 + 8440.50 = 33940.50

⇒ 33940.50 = 25500 × (1 + R / 100)³

⇒ (1 + R / 100)³ = 33940.50 ÷ 25500

⇒ (1 + R / 100)³ = 339405 / 255000

⇒ (1 + R / 100)³ = 1331 / 1000 (dividing by 255)

⇒ (1 + R / 100)³ = (11 / 10)³

⇒ 1 + R / 100 = 11 / 10

⇒ R / 100 = 1 / 10

⇒ R = 10%

⇒ SI = (25500 × 10 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 255 × 30 = 7650

questions.question: Floor of a room measures 4.5 metres × 3 metres. Find the minimum number of complete square marble slabs of equal size required to cover the entire floor.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the minimum number of square slabs, we need the maximum possible size for each slab.

Side of the largest square slab = HCF(4.5 m, 3 m) = 1.5 m

Number of slabs = (Length ÷ Side) × (Breadth ÷ Side)

⇒ Total slabs = (4.5 ÷ 1.5) × (3 ÷ 1.5) = 3 × 2 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 slabs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the floor (L) = 4.5 m = 450 cm

Breadth of the floor (B) = 3 m = 300 cm

**Concept Used:**

To find the minimum number of square slabs, the area of each square slab must be at its maximum.

The maximum side of a square slab that can perfectly fit the dimensions is the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the floor's length and breadth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7001839f2d721a977d84f176561c48050a538fad29bc250075e6c13eb9f0d64.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side of the maximum square slab = HCF(450 cm, 300 cm)

⇒ HCF of 450 and 300 = 150 cm = 1.5 m

⇒ Area of the floor = Length × Breadth = 4.5 m × 3 m = 13.5 m²

⇒ Area of one square slab = Side × Side = 1.5 m × 1.5 m = 2.25 m²

⇒ Minimum number of slabs required = Area of the floor ÷ Area of one square slab

⇒ Number of slabs = 13.5 ÷ 2.25 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 slabs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Minimum Tiles Required

To minimise the number of tiles needed to cover a rectangular area, the tiles used must be as large as possible. The maximum possible side length of a square tile is mathematically equal to the HCF of the length and breadth of the floor.

Number of Tiles Formula

Total number of tiles = (Area of Floor) ÷ (Area of one Tile). Alternatively, it is the product of the number of tiles fitted along the length and the breadth independently.

Greatest Possible Length

When asked to find the greatest possible length that can be used to measure exactly two or more given lengths, always find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of those dimensions.

questions.question: Priyamvada's present age is five years more than twice the age of his cousin Ritika. Sixteen years from now Priyamvada's age will be 150% of that of Ritika's. What is Priyamvada's present age (in years)?
questions.solution:
Let Ritika's present age be "x".

Priyamvada's present age is five years more than twice the age of his cousin Ritika.

∴ Priyamvada's present age = 2x + 5

After 16 years, 

Ritika's age will be "x + 16"

and Priyamvada's age will be "2x + 5 + 16" i.e. 2x + 21.

Priyamvada's age will be 150% of that of Ritika's age.

From the above condition,

2x + 21 = 150% of (x + 16)

(2x + 21) × 100 = 150 × (x + 16)

∴ 200x + 2100 = 150x + 2400

∴ 200x - 150x = 2400 - 2100

∴ 50x = 300

∴ x = 6

Hence, Ritika's present age is 6 years.

Whereas, Priyamvada's present age will be,

(2 × 6) + 5 = 17

Hence, 17 is the correct answer.

• Coastal Plains and Peninsular Plateau **do not block winds**, while the Northern Plains lie **south of the Himalayas** and are affected by this wind barrier.

__
 
• **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**, the **first Prime Minister of India**, famously referred to **Dams** as the **“temples of modern India”** during the inauguration of the **Bhakra-Nangal Dam** in **July 1954**.
 
• He believed that these **multi-purpose river valley projects** would be the foundation for the **economic prosperity** of the country by integrating **agricultural development** with **rapid industrialization**.
 
• The term **"temple"** was used metaphorically to signify that these engineering marvels were the new centers of **worship** for a nation seeking **self-reliance** and **modernity** after centuries of colonial rule.
 
• Nehru envisioned that **Dams** would solve multiple problems simultaneously, including **irrigation for farmers**, **flood control**, and the generation of **hydroelectric power** for burgeoning industries.
 
• The **Bhakra-Nangal project**, located in **Himachal Pradesh** on the **Sutlej River**, served as a symbol of **national pride** and **scientific progress** during the early years of independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Hirakud Dam**, built across the **Mahanadi River** in **Odisha**, was another significant project started during the **First Five-Year Plan**. It holds the record for being the **longest earthen dam** in the world.
 
• The **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)**, established in **1948**, was the first multipurpose river valley project of independent India, inspired by the **Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)** in the **United States**.
 
• The **Tehri Dam** in **Uttarakhand**, located on the **Bhagirathi River**, is currently the **highest dam in India**, standing at a height of **260.5 meters**.
 
 
 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956):**
 
 
• This plan focused heavily on the **primary sector**, specifically **agriculture and irrigation**, to address **food shortages**.
 
• Large-scale investments were made in **Dams** and **irrigation canals** to ensure that **India** could become **self-sufficient in food grains**.
 
 
 
• **Industrialization and Infrastructure:**
 
 
• While Nehru emphasized **Dams**, his vision of modern India also included **Heavy Industries**. During the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)**, major **Steel Plants** were set up in **Bhilai (Chhattisgarh)**, **Rourkela (Odisha)**, and **Durgapur (West Bengal)** with foreign collaboration.
 
• These plants, along with **scientific research institutes**, were also considered part of the broader infrastructure intended to modernize the **Indian economy**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the tidal phenomenon is/are correct?

 
• Tidal waves are characterized by having a longer wavelength but a lower wave height compared to wind-generated waves.
 
• The tidal range refers to the vertical difference between high tide water and low tide water levels.
 
• Tidal bulges are created due to the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on opposite sides of the Earth.
 
• The centrifugal force plays no role in the formation of tidal bulges.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: '1, 2, and 3'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tidal waves are characterized by having a longer wavelength but a lower wave height compared to wind-generated waves.**

 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Tidal waves, or tidal currents, are caused by the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun. These waves have much longer wavelengths (often spanning hundreds of kilometers) and tend to have lower heights compared to waves generated by the wind, which have shorter wavelengths and can have higher wave heights.
 
 
 
• **The tidal range refers to the vertical difference between high tide water and low tide water levels.**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The tidal range is indeed the vertical difference between the highest high tide and the lowest low tide. It is a crucial aspect of tidal behavior that is influenced by the relative positions of the Earth, moon, and sun.
 
 
 
• **Tidal bulges are created due to the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on opposite sides of the Earth.**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Tidal bulges are formed due to the gravitational forces exerted by the moon and the sun. On the side of the Earth facing the moon, the water is pulled towards the moon, creating a high tide. On the opposite side, the inertia of the water causes another high tide. The sun also affects tidal bulges, but its influence is less than that of the moon.
 
 
 
• **The centrifugal force plays no role in the formation of tidal bulges.**
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**.
 
• The centrifugal force is indeed an important factor in the formation of tidal bulges. As the Earth and the moon revolve around their common center of mass, the centrifugal force acts outward and contributes to the creation of a tidal bulge on the side of the Earth opposite the moon.
 
 

**Hence the Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct, and Statement 4 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tidal Phenomena:**__

 
 
• **Spring Tides:** These occur when the Earth, moon, and sun are aligned, resulting in higher high tides and lower low tides due to the combined gravitational forces of the moon and the sun.
 
• **Neap Tides:** These occur when the Earth, moon, and sun form a right angle. The gravitational forces of the moon and the sun counteract each other, resulting in lower high tides and higher low tides.
 
• **Tidal Currents:** Tidal currents are the horizontal flow of water that accompanies the rising and falling of the tide. These currents are influenced by the shape of the coastline and the depth of the water body.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** The gravitational force exerted by the moon is the primary driver of tidal phenomena. The sun's gravitational force, although significant, has a lesser effect due to the greater distance from the Earth.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps in blood clotting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin K**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Vitamin K** plays a critical role in blood clotting by activating proteins and calcium essential for the clotting process. 
• The primary function of Vitamin K is to synthesize **prothrombin**, a protein and clotting factor crucial for blood coagulation. 
• Deficiency of Vitamin K can lead to excessive bleeding or hemorrhaging as the blood fails to clot properly. 
• Vitamin K is naturally present in green leafy vegetables such as **spinach, kale, and broccoli**, and is also synthesized by bacteria in the human gut. 
• Vitamin K is fat-soluble, meaning it is absorbed along with dietary fats and stored in the body's fatty tissues and liver. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Vitamin K Types:** 
• **Vitamin K1 (Phylloquinone):** Found in plant-based foods, especially green leafy vegetables. 
• **Vitamin K2 (Menaquinone):** Found in animal products and fermented foods, and also produced by gut bacteria. 
• Both forms are essential, but K1 is primarily responsible for blood clotting, while K2 is linked to bone and cardiovascular health. 
• **Other Functions of Vitamin K:** 
• Vitamin K is also important for bone health as it helps in the regulation of calcium in the body. 
• It prevents calcification in blood vessels, reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases. 
• **Deficiency Symptoms:** 
• Prolonged bleeding or bruising. 
• Internal bleeding, especially in newborns (neonatal hemorrhage). 
• Bone weakness due to impaired calcium regulation. 
• **Risk Factors for Deficiency:** 
• Newborns are at higher risk due to low Vitamin K stores at birth, which is why they are often given Vitamin K injections. 
• Adults with conditions affecting fat absorption, such as celiac disease or Crohn’s disease, may also be at risk. 
• Long-term use of antibiotics can disrupt gut bacteria responsible for producing Vitamin K. 
• **Comparison with Other Vitamins:** 
• **Vitamin C:** Involved in immune function and collagen synthesis, but not in clotting. 
• **Vitamin D:** Important for calcium and phosphorus metabolism, promoting bone health. 
• **Vitamin A:** Essential for vision, immune system, and cell growth.

__
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspot Classification:** The Western Ghats are officially recognized as one of the world's top biodiversity hotspots due to their extremely high levels of species diversity and endemism.
 
• **Rich Flora and Fauna:** This mountain range is home to thousands of plant and animal species, many of which are unique to the region. It supports a variety of ecosystems ranging from tropical rainforests to montane forests.

Cloud computing is internet-based computing where customers do not own the physical infrastructure. All services are on internet. Various services in cloud computing model are as follows:

questions.question: In data transmission ______ is the amount of data moved successfully from one place to another in a given time period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Throughput.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Throughput** refers to the rate at which a system, process, or network can transfer data, perform operations, or deliver results within a given period of time. It is often used to measure the efficiency and capacity of various systems.
 
• Measuring Throughput: Throughput is typically measured in bits per second (**bps**), kilobits per second (**Kbps**), megabits per second (**Mbps**), or gigabits per second (**Gbps**), depending on the speed of the network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Word length **typically refers to the number of bits in a data unit that is processed as a single entity by the hardware or software. The word length can vary depending on the specific context and the type of system or protocol being used.
 
• **Bandwidth** typically refers to the maximum data transfer rate of a network or internet connection. It is usually measured in bits per second (bps), kilobits per second (Kbps), megabits per second (Mbps), or gigabits per second (Gbps). For example, if you have a home internet connection with a bandwidth of 100 Mbps, it means the maximum data transfer rate is 100 megabits per second.
 
• **Queue size** represents the maximum number of packets that can be stored in the buffer queue at any given time. It is typically measured in terms of the number of packets or the amount of memory allocated for buffering. For example, a router might have a queue size of 100 packets for a particular interface.

questions.question: A student preparing a report notices that the same formatting errors appear across multiple pages. To apply consistent design rules and easily update them, what feature of a word processor should they use?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Styles and Themes.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Styles and Themes** are features in a word processor that allow users to apply consistent formatting to text across a document.
 
• Using these features, you can define and apply a specific font, size, color, alignment, and other formatting properties to headings, paragraphs, and other elements.
 
• **Benefits:** They help maintain a uniform design throughout the document and make it easier to update the formatting. For example, changing the style of a heading will automatically update all headings in the document.
 
• Styles and Themes can be accessed in most word processors through the toolbar or menu, often under the "Home" or "Design" tab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Document Encryption:** This is a security feature that protects a document by requiring a password to access it. It is unrelated to formatting or design consistency.
 
• **Find and Replace:** This tool is used to search for specific text and replace it with new text, but it is not designed for applying consistent formatting to a document.

questions.question: In Relative Cell Reference in MS-Excel 365, if we copy the formula '=A4*B4' from cells E4 to E5, the formula in E5 is adjusted by one column to the right and becomes ______ goes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**=A5*B5**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Relative** **cell references** in Excel are **automatically adjusted when a formula is moved or copied to different cells**.
 
• When we copy the formula '=A4B4' from cell E4 to E5, Excel increments the row part of each reference in the formula by 1, because we moved the formula down one row.
 
• It doesn't shift the references right since we didn't move the formula horizontally.
 
• Thus, the formula in cell E5 becomes '=A5B5'.

questions.question:
Identify the correct order of the following list of computer components ranked from slowest to fastest in terms of access time.

A. CPU cache

B. RAM

C. SSD

D. Optical Drive

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is__ D, C, B, A__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****The order of access time for computer components**

__
 
• **Optical Drive**

 
 
• An optical drive is the slowest among the listed components. It uses laser technology to read and write data, which is significantly slower compared to solid-state and volatile memories.
 
 
 
• **SSD (Solid State Drive)**
 
 
• SSDs are much faster than optical drives but are slower compared to RAM and CPU cache. They use flash memory to store data, providing quicker access times than traditional hard disk drives.
 
 
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)**
 
 
• RAM is a volatile memory that provides fast access to data that the CPU needs while performing tasks. It is faster than SSDs but slower than the CPU cache.
 
 
 
• **CPU Cache**
 
 
• The CPU cache is the fastest memory type among the listed components. It is a small-sized type of volatile computer memory that provides high-speed data access to the CPU, significantly reducing the time it takes to access frequently used data.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Access Time Comparison

 
 
• Access time is a critical factor in determining the performance of a computer system. Faster access times lead to better system performance.
 
• The hierarchy of memory access speed is essential for optimizing computer architecture and ensuring efficient data processing.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement[s] is/are true?

 [1] Registers are the fastest type of memory located inside the CPU

 [2] Secondary memory is directly accessible by the CPU without any intermediate memory
questions.solution:
Registers are the fastest memory, followed by cache memory, which is faster than RAM. Registers are located inside the CPU and hold data for immediate processing.

**Secondary memory** [e.g., hard disk, SSD, USB drive] is **not directly accessible by the CPU**.Data from secondary memory must first be **loaded into primary memory [RAM]** before the CPU can access and process it.

questions.question:
Identify True/False from the following statements.

A. In Windows 10, Windows logo key + L is the keyboard shortcut to lock your PC.

B. In Windows, the keyboard shortcut for copying is Ctrl+C.

C. The Windows 'Start' button is found in the title bar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1) A-True, B-True, C-False**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement A - True:** ✅ Pressing **Windows logo key + L** on your keyboard locks your PC or switches users. This is a quick and secure way to prevent unauthorized access when you step away.
 
• **Statement B - True:** ✅ **Ctrl + C** is the universally accepted keyboard shortcut for copying selected text, files, or other items to the clipboard in Windows and most other operating systems.
 
• **Statement C - False:** ❌ The **Start** button is found on the **Taskbar**, typically at the bottom-left corner of the screen, not in the **Title bar**. The title bar is part of an application window and displays the window's name and control buttons (minimize, maximize, close).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taskbar:** It houses the Start button, system tray, and pinned applications. It's used for launching and managing running programs.
 
• **Title bar:** Appears at the top of every application window and includes the name of the application or document along with window controls.
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts:** Improve efficiency. For example, Ctrl+V is for paste, Ctrl+Z for undo, and Ctrl+X for cut.

**Hence, the correct answer is:** **option 1) A-True, B-True, C-False**
